transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I spend so much time checking and rechecking how I look at the gym and before going out that it’s taking over my days. It has gotten to the point where it's completely overwhelming, and I feel like I can't control it anymore.

Are you checking these things because you are afraid that something bad will happen if you don't, or is it primarily because you are intensely preoccupied with a perceived flaw in your physical appearance?

It’s entirely because of how I look. I’m obsessed with how crooked my face and jawline look from the side, so I constantly check mirrors and change clothes to try and hide that messed-up side before anyone else can see it.
How much time each day do you spend performing these checking behaviors or trying to hide these features, and does this significantly interfere with your work, school, or social life?

I easily spend an hour or more at a time checking reflections, fixing my hair, and changing clothes to try to hide the messed-up side of my face. Because of this, I’ve been showing up late or missing shifts at work, and I’ve canceled so many soccer games and salsa nights that my sister and friends complain I’m never around anymore.
